neighbours.label: the quantity word right before a population of people in social and economic statistics (the average ___ household, middle-___ families, 2,000 average ___ homes), predicting 'families/Americans', as against the same statistical phrasing about things
fire: Higher gas prices will cost the average household about 300 dollars.
The tax cut saves the average worker very little money.
Methane from the farm powers 1,500 average homes every year.
Rising rents are squeezing middle-class families across the city.
The plan would raise taxes on the average American by two percent.
Inflation has eroded the buying power of the average consumer.
Polls show the average voter pays little attention to budgets.
Lead pipes still serve hundreds of thousands of residents in the state.
quiet: Higher fuel prices will raise the average price of a flight.
The new tires barely change the average mileage of the truck.
Methane from the farm powers three large factories every year.
Rising rents are squeezing small bookshops across the city.
The plan would raise the average interest rate by two percent.
Inflation has eroded the value of the average government bond.
Records show the average rainfall has dropped every spring.
Lead pipes still run under hundreds of streets in the state.
